title: Moleche Fritte
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Venice's celebrated soft-shell crabs, harvested during their brief molting window and fried whole in a light egg batter, eaten entirely, shell and all.
longDesc: Moleche are small lagoon crabs caught precisely during the narrow window after they shed their hard shell and before the new one hardens, a fleeting seasonal specialty that Venetian fishermen have tracked and harvested for generations.
ingredients: 500 g (1.1 lb) live soft-shell crabs (moleche), cleaned
steps: Rinse the cleaned crabs and pat dry.
Dip each crab in the beaten egg, then dredge lightly in flour.
Fry the crabs in batches for 3–4 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and season with salt.
Serve immediately, hot, with lemon wedges — the entire crab, shell included, is eaten.
chefTips: Genuine moleche are only available during their brief molting season, making this a true seasonal delicacy.
Fry at a properly hot temperature to ensure the crabs cook through and crisp quickly.
These are eaten whole, shell and all, which is only possible because the shell is still soft.
commonMistakes: Using crabs that have already hardened their new shell, which won't have the desired tender, edible texture.
Frying at too low a temperature, resulting in greasy rather than crisp crabs.
Overcrowding the pan, which can cause uneven cooking.
storage: Best eaten immediately; not suited to storage.
reheating: Not recommended; best enjoyed fresh and hot.
healthBenefits: A good source of lean protein.
culturalNote: Moleche are one of Venice's most prized and fleeting seasonal delicacies, harvested from the lagoon during a narrow window each spring and autumn when the crabs have shed their shells.
